title: Weekly poll results: touchscreens on laptops only make sense if you can use the laptop as a tablet
description: The results from last week’s poll show that touchscreens do have a place on some laptops. It’s mainly the ones with a 360° hinge or the ones where the screen can detach from the keyboard – in other words, the laptops that can be used as a tablet. According to commenters, a touchscreen enables quick and easy navigation – especially for people who don’t like using a touchpad. Also, it has clear applications for artists, designers and developers. title: vivo X500 Ultra on track to launch next year, says tipster
description: Tipster Digital Chat Station recently said that the Oppo Find X10 Ultra is on hold and might not launch. Before that, we heard Xiaomi had canceled the 18 Ultra. This left some wondering whether vivo would also cancel its X500 Ultra, despite vivo's VP of Product confirming that the smartphone would arrive next year in March or April in China. That confirmation came in September, and plans can always change. The good news is, the vivo X500 Ultra is still on track. title: Deals: Galaxy S26 Ultra and S25 Ultra on sale, Galaxy Z Fold8 price drops
description: Patience pays off – some flagships were holding a fairly high price last week, but now they are down to a much better number. That is the case for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra – a 256GB unit was $1,105 last week, now it’s $1,000. We’ve seen it as low as $950 not too long ago, but the $50 difference isn’t huge. title: OnePlus releases its ColorOS 17 rollout schedule for November
description: With ColorOS 17, OnePlus officially kickstarts the transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS, but not all devices are running the latest version of the software based on Android 17. After the company updated the OnePlus 15 in late October, it's now time for the older models. The company released the update schedule for November, listing all the devices that are about to receive ColorOS 17. The first one that already got the update is the OnePlus 13R - two days ago on November 5. If you still haven't received the update, wait a few more days, as it might be a staged rollout. title: Google to add vocabulary for corrected words to Gboard's Rambler voice typing feature
description: Android Authority app teardown reveals some cool new features coming to Gboard's AI-powered voice typing feature called Rambler. Rambler, however, is a Pixel-exclusive functionality, at least for now, and makes voice typing that much easier. It can leave out pauses or other filler words, but it can't remember corrected words or slang from your personal vocabulary. That's about to change, though. title: Xiaomi 18 might actually arrive this year, 3C reveals the charging capabilities
description: The Xiaomi 18 Pro series was announced in China in September, and the company confirmed that the duo is going global by the end of this year. In fact, we expect the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max to hit the global market as early as this month. However, the conversation left out the vanilla Xiaomi 18 entirely, stirring speculation that we won't be getting a Xiaomi 17 successor this year. A 3C listing suggests otherwise, and it appears to be in line with earlier rumors that the Xiaomi 18 will arrive at a later date, probably sometime in December. title: WhatsApp is testing a feature that lets you control who sees your phone number
description: WhatsApp introduced the Username feature in June. It hasn't been fully rolled out yet, but users can already reserve their usernames. WhatsApp introduced usernames with a focus on privacy, allowing its users to communicate without knowing each other's phone numbers. Building on that, WhatsApp is now testing a feature that grants users granular control over their phone number visibility. This revelation comes from WABetaInfo, which discovered the development in beta version 2.26.45.1 of WhatsApp for Android. title: We now have a more definite timeframe for Samsung Galaxy Buds On's Europe launch
description: The Samsung Galaxy Buds On wireless earphones, unveiled last month, are currently only available in South Korea and the US. Samsung said the Buds On would come to Europe in early 2027 without getting specific. Well, we now have a more definite timeframe for the Galaxy Buds On's European debut. Citing their sources, SamMobile claims the Samsung Galaxy Buds On will launch in Europe in the third week of 2027. We still don't have the launch date, but at least we now have a more definite launch timeframe. The Galaxy Buds On are Samsung's first clip-on earphones. They are priced at...

title: iOS 27 users report HDMI output issues and there's no fix in sight
description: As is usually the case with new software releases, rollouts rarely go smoothly, and developers work overtime to provide fixes. One problem that gained a lot of traction is the Apple Intelligence storage issue that occupies about 15GB in some cases, even if you don't use AI or it's not available at all in your country. At least there's a workaround that seems to work until Apple addresses it. The same cannot be said about this annoying bug causing problems with the HDMI output. title: New Realme 17 Pro spec leak helps clarify its place in the upcoming lineup
description: Some key specs for an upcoming Realme 17 Pro-series phone leaked last month, but its identity wasn't clear - it could have been either the Pro or the Pro+. Today, a new report citing industry sources specifically details the Realme 17 Pro, and the differences suggest the earlier leak may have described its higher-end sibling. The 17 Pro will allegedly come with a 1.5K AMOLED screen with a 120Hz refresh rate, the Dimensity 7300 chipset, a 50MP main camera, and an 8MP ultrawide. The selfie camera will support 4K video recording at 30fps, although its resolution is unclear - it could be...

title: Future iPhones will have one less button, new rumor claims
description: Apple introduced the Action button with the iPhone 15 Pro, and the iPhone 18 Pro still has it. Now, a tipster on Weibo claims the company is planning to combine the Action button and the Camera Control into a single button on next year's iPhones. The dedicated Action button will allegedly start disappearing from new iPhones in the second half of 2027. Its functions will move to the Camera Control, with a single press opening the Camera app and a long press triggering the shortcut assigned to the Action button. The tipster specifically stresses that it's the Action button going away, not...

title: Airbnb is building an AI travel agent that designs its own interface
description: Airbnb has spent much of 2026 folding AI into search, listing descriptions, and customer support. Now, in its Q3 2026 shareholder letter, the company says it's building a specialized AI agent meant to help guests plan and book trips, with a rollout planned for the first half of 2027. Airbnb doesn't think a traditional chatbot is the right way to plan a trip. Instead, it's developing a custom, AI-native experience that "builds the interface around your question." title: Apple says over 100,000 apps are now optimized for the iPhone Duo
description: The iPhone Duo started shipping about two weeks ago, and app support has been one of the early talking points. Today, Apple claims there are already well over 100,000 apps built for the foldable live on the App Store, with thousands of optimized titles being added each day. [#InlinePriceWidget,13804,1#] Susan Prescott, Apple's vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, says developers have moved quickly to embrace the handset. title: Samsung Display tipped to lead OLED supply for 2027 iPad Air
description: The latest versions of the iPad Pro and iPad mini already sport OLED screens, but the current 11-inch and 13-inch iPad Air are stuck with LCD panels. Today, industry sources in Korea are claiming that the first OLED iPad Air models are due in the first half of 2027 - which lines up with earlier reporting. These Korean sources put 2027 OLED iPad shipment outlooks at 3 to 4 million Pro units, 4 to 5 million mini units, and 4 to 5 million Air units. description: According to a new rumor, Samsung's upcoming Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra will stick to Snapdragon chipsets in South Korea, despite the Exynos 2700 reportedly outperforming Qualcomm's offering in internal tests. title: Oppo's first gimbal camera is almost ready to take on DJI and Insta360
description: Oppo confirmed last September that it was working on a new form-factor imaging product line for release in 2026, and earlier this year Digital Chat Station said the project was internally known as Fuyao - a pocket gimbal camera meant to take on DJI's Osmo Pocket line. Today, the tipster says Fuyao should be arriving soon, and that there's high confidence about the product's success inside the company. title: WhatsApp announces Events Home and shareable event invites
description: WhatsApp users can already create events in a 1:1 conversation and group chats. Now they can also create events that they can share with people who don't have a WhatsApp account. "Create an event, add a cover photo, share the link, and they can see details and RSVP without downloading the app," said WhatsApp in a blog post. The company also said your phone number won't be shown to event guests you don't know, and guests without a WhatsApp account will only see the event address after they RSVP. title: Oppo Find X10 Ultra has reportedly been cancelled
description: Oppo's Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max went global recently, and the Find X10 Ultra was expected to follow in the first half of next year as the camera-focused top dog. Today, Digital Chat Station on Weibo says Oppo's Ultra project is on hold. There's no reason given, but it's easy to guess that it all has to do with the insane memory prices which would have pushed the Find X10 Ultra to stratospheric levels, considering it was supposed to be a camera-centric flagship, and those cameras aren't cheap either. description: Since Huawei unveiled the Pura X View earlier this year, several Chinese smartphone brands, including Oppo, Honor, and most recently Xiaomi, have been rumored to be developing their own wide-screen phones. Now, a new leak suggests that vivo is also joining the race. According to tipster Digital Chat Station, vivo is targeting a 2027 launch for its first wide-screen candybar-style smartphone.
